paragraphs.title: David Remains in Jerusalem and Encounters Bathsheba

answers: Jerusalem
Rabbah
The battlefield

A woman washing herself
Joab

answers: Bath-sheba, the daughter of Eliam
Joab’s wife
The wife of one of David’s servants

easy.q: Who was the woman David saw?

answers: She went immediately to battle
She became queen
She conceived and told David
medium.explanation: The woman conceived and sent to tell David that she was with child.
medium.q: What happened after Bath-sheba came unto David?

answers: The beginning of winter
The time when kings went forth to battle
The end of David’s life
medium.explanation: It refers to the season when kings went forth to battle.

answers: David saw Bath-sheba, sent for her, and she conceived
There was a battle, Joab died, and David married
Bath-sheba conceived, David saw her, and she went to battle

answers: David was in Jerusalem while his army was at war
Joab was in Jerusalem while David was at war
Bath-sheba was at war while Uriah was at home

answers: She was Uriah’s wife
She sent and told David that she was with child
She was washing on the roof
challenge.explanation: Her message directly informed David of the pregnancy after their encounter.
challenge.q: Which detail connects Bath-sheba’s pregnancy with her meeting David?

answers: He knew she was unknown
He learned her identity and family situation
He asked Joab to bring her from the battlefield
challenge.explanation: David learned that she was Bath-sheba, the wife of Uriah the Hittite.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David’s inquiry about the woman before sending for her?

paragraphs.title: David’s Attempts to Conceal the Pregnancy

answers: Uriah the Hittite
Bath-sheba
The men of Rabbah
easy.explanation: David said, “Send me Uriah the Hittite.”
easy.q: Whom did David command Joab to send to him?

answers: Go forth to Rabbah
Go down to his house and wash his feet
Bring Joab to him
easy.explanation: David told Uriah, “Go down to thy house, and wash thy feet.”
easy.q: What did David tell Uriah to do?

answers: Yes, that evening
Yes, after David made him drunk
No
easy.explanation: Uriah slept at the king’s door and did not go down to his house.
easy.q: Did Uriah go down to his house?

answers: So Uriah could become a captain
So the pregnancy might be attributed to Uriah
So Uriah could send a message to Joab
medium.explanation: David wanted Uriah to be with his wife so the pregnancy would appear to be his.
medium.q: Why did David want Uriah to return home?

answers: A portion or gift of food from the king
A secret letter to Joab
A weapon of war
medium.explanation: It was food sent from the king after Uriah left the palace.
medium.q: In this context, what was “a mess of meat from the king”?

answers: He was angry with David
The ark, Israel, and Judah were in tents or the camp
He did not know where his house was
medium.explanation: Uriah would not enjoy his home while the army and the ark remained in the field.
medium.q: Why did Uriah refuse to go down to his house?

answers: He was loyal to the army and his fellow servants
He wanted to leave the war
He planned to rebel against Joab
challenge.explanation: Uriah emphasized the condition of the army and refused personal comfort.
challenge.q: What does Uriah’s answer reveal about his character?

answers: He immediately gave up
He tried to persuade Uriah by making him drunk
He sent Bath-sheba to the camp
challenge.explanation: David made Uriah drunk, but Uriah still did not go down to his house.
challenge.q: How did David change his attempt after Uriah refused to go home?

answers: Uriah’s refusal prevented the pregnancy from being attributed to him
His words caused the army to retreat
His words brought Bath-sheba to the camp
challenge.explanation: Because Uriah did not go to his wife, David could not conceal the pregnancy in that way.
challenge.q: How did Uriah’s words cause David’s plan to fail?

Uriah
Bath-sheba

Uriah’s hand
A messenger from Rabbah

He became king
He died

Set Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle and retire from him
Protect Uriah at all costs

A place outside the camp
The king’s house

He sent Uriah back to Jerusalem
He hid Uriah in the camp

The letter was sent to Bath-sheba

Joab did not take part in the fighting

Uriah won the battle, so David sent him home
Bath-sheba went to war, so Joab withdrew

answers: Bath-sheba
Joab
Uriah
easy.explanation: Joab sent a messenger to David.

answers: The course of the battle and Uriah’s death
David’s marriage to Bath-sheba
The army’s return to Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The messenger told David about the battle and reported that Uriah was dead.

He imprisoned the messenger

easy.q: How did David respond to the report of Uriah’s death?

To ask David to build a wall
To announce that the city had been captured

After the messenger has finished reporting all the battle details
When the messenger leaves the army

That Uriah should enter his house

As Uriah’s personal victory
As an act committed by Bath-sheba

Joab announced a marriage, and David changed his order

answers: “Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also”
“David tarried still at Jerusalem”
“The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents”
challenge.explanation: The messenger specifically called Uriah “thy servant.”

answers: She went to battle
She mourned for her husband
She left Jerusalem
easy.q: What did Bath-sheba do when she heard that Uriah was dead?

He sent Bath-sheba to Rabbah
He appointed Uriah captain

easy.q: What did David do after the mourning was past?

answers: A daughter
A son
No child
easy.explanation: The KJV says that she “bare him a son.”
easy.q: What did Bath-sheba bear to David?

answers: Bath-sheba became David’s wife
Bath-sheba returned to Uriah
David went to battle alone
medium.explanation: David fetched Bath-sheba to his house, and she became his wife.

answers: A period of sorrow for the dead
A celebration after victory
A military command
medium.explanation: Mourning is the period of sorrow following Uriah’s death.
medium.q: What does “mourning” mean in this passage?

David appeared to lose, but the LORD called it victory
Bath-sheba appeared to go to war, but the LORD stopped her
medium.explanation: Although David married Bath-sheba after Uriah’s death, the LORD was displeased with the deed.

answers: The LORD approved all David’s actions
The LORD regarded David’s actions as wrong and sinful
The LORD did not know what had happened
challenge.explanation: The final statement plainly says that the LORD was displeased with David’s deed.
challenge.q: What is the meaning of “the thing that David had done displeased the LORD”?

Victory, celebration, and Uriah’s promotion
Bath-sheba’s departure, David’s death, and peace
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from mourning to marriage and then declares the LORD’s displeasure.
challenge.q: Which sequence emphasizes the moral problem at the end of the chapter?

answers: Adultery and bloodshed
Theft and exile
Idolatry and strife
challenge.explanation: David’s actions involved taking another man’s wife and arranging the man’s death.
challenge.q: Which two grave wrongs are represented by David’s actions in this account?
